1	# Agent design
2	
3	The target architecture of our buyer, merged from the team's planning notes (PRs #7 to #10,
4	10 Oct). What we learned in play is in `learnings.md`; this file says what we build.
5	
6	**Status.** The branch `steffen/price-engine` plays a code-only policy with a model-written
7	paragraph (`buyer/policy.py`, run by `buyer/runner.py`): practice mean of best scores 0.73 (from
8	0.32), sandbox D01 0.99, D02 0.73. What it does is under "Implemented" below; the rest of this file
9	is the target design. Julian's draft two (`origin/julian/draft-two`) holds a richer stance and
10	reader design that is not merged. The architecture diagram is on page 1 of
11	[how-it-works.pdf](how-it-works.pdf).
12	
13	## Implemented (price engine)
14	
15	| Module | Job |
16	|---|---|
17	| `buyer/economics.py` | C of a sheet; the accept gate (`deal_cost`); what a sheet is worth to the supplier (`supplier_value` plus overtime for a faster delivery than it quoted); term planning: every allowed combination priced at the supplier's own valuation, lowest C, ties to the supplier's side; the relationship-optimal price |
18	| `buyer/claims.py` | claim bank: should-cost below its price, our order prices, falling cost-driver indices, notice period, forecast, scorecard, case rival quotes, hedge and open-book notes; rival offers in an RFQ |
19	| `buyer/personas.py` | owner type, persona signals from notes, letters, quote remarks and news, cost of money |
20	| `buyer/policy.py` | per thread: anchor by goal and persona, 30 % of the gap per round, held low after a deep first concession, patience budget for near-cost, fully booked and relationship-goal suppliers; adopts its counter terms when they cost us less, mirrors a better alternative, takes a required index clause; claims 3 in round 1, then 1 per round; close on final offer, agreement or round limit |
21	| `buyer/reader.py` | the supplier's asks from its fixed sentences (volume, proof, faster payment, our target); no model |
22	| `buyer/writer.py`, `buyer/llm.py` | the e-mail: a model paragraph that answers the supplier's last e-mail and its asks (no digits, IDs or leaks, else the template), then code sentences with figures (the binding volume), claims and the proposal from code; the forecast rows as a CSV when proof is asked |
23	| `buyer/runner.py` | one message at a time per session, to the thread whose 60 s clock has run longest; keepalive questions for finished bidders; rollback when a send times out; a guarded move resends our last sheet; the model's time budgeted so every live clock still gets a message; a terminal reply ends the case; accept the cheapest standing sheet that keeps the must-haves and beats the alternative (relationship charge included), after a refused close decide again on what stands; Live Final waves that never raise and resume a crashed case |
24	
25	## Principle
26	
27	Code owns every number and every binding decision; the model reads replies and writes e-mails.
28	Score is total cost C, not price. Every step has a fallback that still sends a move within 60 s.
29	
30	## A case
31	
32	1. **Prepare** (before the first move, about 20 s): open the session, build a case brief: C_open,
33	   C_alt, target, walk-away, the lever table (C of each allowed option), a view of each supplier,
34	   and a claim bank of verified arguments. A stance call proposes per-supplier parameters; code
35	   clamps them.
36	2. **Negotiate**, one thread negotiator per supplier, in parallel. Each round:
37	
38	   ```
39	   supplier reply
40	     -> READ    (model, hard timeout)  offer, intent, objections, statements
41	     -> CHECK   (code)  supplier statements against the data
42	     -> PLAN    (code)  candidate sheets scored with total_cost, filtered by must_haves_ok
43	     -> DECIDE  (code)  counter / accept / walk away, move size, claims
44	     -> WRITE   (model, hard timeout; template if late)  figures and IDs injected by code
45	     -> GUARD   (code)  every negotiable field, claim format, no leaks, no unplanned figures
46	   ```
47	
48	3. **Close**: accept the best sheet that keeps every must-have and beats C_alt, or walk away;
49	   at the latest 90 s before the wave's 8-minute cap.
50	4. **Learn**: store the trace and what we learned per supplier for the next practice run.
51	
52	## Modules
53	
54	| Module | Job | Run by |
55	|---|---|---|
56	| Runner | polls the final's case list, one coordinator per case, restarts after a crash | code |
57	| Coordinator | case brief, starts thread negotiators, shared state, decides when to close | code |
58	| Economics | C of any sheet, floor, anchor, target, concession steps, accept gate | code |
59	| Personas | one profile per supplier: traits with evidence, levers, history | model offline, code live |
60	| Claim bank | arguments as sentences with figure and data ID, computed as the arena checks them | code |
61	| Reader / writer | supplier e-mail to JSON; move to e-mail | small model, hard timeout |
62	| Fact check | supplier statements: confirmed, contradicted, selective, unverifiable (not built) | code |
63	| Guard | blocks leaks, unknown IDs, unplanned figures, broken must-haves | code |
64	| Fallback cascade | unknown supplier or part: case facts, data search, category averages, its documents | code |

71	| 2 | supplier cost floor | anchor, target, relationship charge | `should_cost`, cost-breakdown XLSX on request |
72	| 3 | index values of its cost drivers | justified price change, strongest claims | `cost_drivers`, `index_values`, `facts.json` |
73	| 4 | letters, notes, news | what moves it (cash, capacity, relationship), notice periods | `documents`, `correspondence/`, `news` |
74	| 5 | negotiation history | how far it usually moves | `negotiation_history` |
75	| 6 | intel, our invoices | archetype, payment lever | `supplier_intel`, `invoices`, `suppliers` (cash discount) |
76	| 7 | contracts and clauses | notice, index clauses, expiry, single sourcing | `contracts`, `contract_clauses`, `sourcing` |
77	| 8 | scorecards, QNs | quality lever | `scorecards`, `quality_notifications` |
78	| 9 | forecasts, PO prices, rival quotes | volume, price history, rival arguments | `forecast_lines`, `po_lines`, `quotes` |

82	## Supplier estimate
83	
84	`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` prices a deal for the supplier from `standard`, `interest_rate`,
85	`ppm` and `extra`; `relationship_cost` needs `full_cost` and is 0 without it. So we estimate:
86	
87	- **Full cost**: cost-breakdown XLSX, else `should_cost` moved by its drivers' index change, else
88	  quote minus an assumed margin. A relationship charge in a practice result reveals the true margin.
89	- **Cost of money**: cash discounts, cash-need notes, credit index, equity ratio. Seen rates: 0 to
90	  17 %/yr (`learnings.md`).
91	- **Extra**: overtime for speed (negative) or idle capacity filled by volume (positive), only from
92	  evidence. Volume, contract length and index clauses are not cash in `supplier_value`.
93	
94	C_best estimate: the cheapest allowed sheet whose supplier value stays above its floor, or C_alt.
95	
96	## Policy
97	
98	A stance per supplier (opening gap, capture, margin, justified share, steps) proposed by the model
99	at case open, clamped by code to a range per tier and goal, logged with a reason. Fallback
100	constants when the stance call times out:
101	
102	| Constant | Values |
103	|---|---|
104	| capture (share of possible saving before accepting) | leverage 0.75, quality_first 0.65, stabilise 0.6, secure_supply 0.55, routine 0.5 |
105	| opening gap below the quote (never below the floor) | strategic 5 %, important 8 %, standard 12 % |
106	| margin above full cost for the floor | case's `sustainable_margin_pct` in `stabilise` / `secure_supply`, else strategic 4 %, important 2 %, standard 0 % |
107	| justified share offered in round 1 of a price increase | strategic 0.5, important 0.25, standard 0 |
108	| concession steps, only after the supplier moved | 35, 25, 15, 10 % of the remaining gap |
109	
110	Live signals adjust within bounds: approval needed shrinks steps (x0.7), high walk risk stops
111	price pushes. At the target, hold one more round while the supplier still moves.
112	
113	## Build order
114	
115	1. Accept and walk-away guard with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`.
116	2. Term search: every combination of allowed options, scored with standard terms for unstated
117	   fields. Fixes coverage and index-clause losses.
118	3. Supplier estimate: full cost and cost of money, giving target and walk-away.
119	4. Claim bank from `facts.json` and the index tables.
120	5. Persona reading and pacing.
121	6. Tune on practice traces, one change per batch.
122	
123	## Generalise
124	
125	- Branch on features (goal, must-haves, credit, cash signals, owner type, quote content), never on
126	  case or supplier IDs. No constants copied from one case.
127	- Hold out two or three practice cases for checking only.
128	- Test failure paths: late model call, malformed reply, a supplier that refuses everything,
129	  missing quote fields, a quote PDF without a standard-terms section.
130	- Change the agent only for a lesson seen in two cases or clearly general. Freeze early.
131	
132	## Tactics
133	
134	Use: data-backed anchors, requests framed as trades, two or three packages to watch the choice,
135	shrinking concessions with an ask in return, real rival offers cited by ID, a recap of every field
136	before closing.
137	
138	Avoid: invented figures or rival offers (`contradicted`), bluffed urgency or walk-aways (no
139	effect, `learnings.md`), squeezing a weak supplier in `stabilise` / `secure_supply`, leaking
140	urgency, budget, target or a missing alternative. Prompt injection of supplier bots counts as an
141	attack on the arena: never.

14	## Takeaways for the agent
15	
16	1. **Stay below the supplier's counter until the end; it agrees the moment our sheet reaches the
17	   counter it would make.** D01: our 51.25 one cent under its 51.30 was agreed at once
18	   (sandbox `14ea35524959126f`). Moving a share of the gap each round keeps it conceding: the
19	   engine took the practice mean of best scores from 0.32 to 0.73.
20	2. **Verified claims that it "took into account" lower where it stops, most of all in round 1.**
21	   D01 with the same price path: no claims 50.00, delivery record 49.60, notice 49.60, should-cost
22	   49.30, three claims spread over rounds 48.90 (score 0.998). Which types count differs by
23	   supplier (table under Arguments and claims).
24	3. **Words move it too.** D01, identical sheets, no claims: plain 50.00, "firm" 49.90, warm and
25	   acknowledging its wage costs 49.60, "What would you need from us to move further on the
26	   price?" 49.40 (0.987). But a question repeated every round backfires: practice suppliers
27	   answered "volume!" where volume is fixed and stopped moving (P05, P18 v3). Answer what it
28	   asked; state a fixed volume as our full demand, with the figure.
29	4. **Patience is a budget of about 40 % cumulative gap** (sum over rounds of our sheet's distance
30	   to its counter, relative to its price): final offers at 41 to 42 % (D01 linear paths), 39 %
31	   (P07), 42 % (P08), 36 % (P18). Suppliers selling near our should-cost or with a pricing
32	   committee end much earlier: Nordmark walked away at 19 % (P02 v1), Ravensteiner gave its final
33	   offer in round 1 at a 15 % gap (P10 v1).
34	5. **Choose terms by C at the supplier's own valuation**, including a contract beyond our horizon
35	   (free for us, security for it) and the overtime a fully booked supplier charges for faster
36	   delivery (about 0.5 % of the price per day: Hrvelec, Ravensteiner). This alone moved P10 from
37	   a 42-day to a 56-day lead time.
38	6. **In relationship goals stop at the price where C is lowest.** D01: all claims at once pushed
39	   to 48.50 and scored 0.969; stopping near 48.90 scored 0.998, the relationship charge grows
40	   faster below.
41	7. **Only a supplier's standing sheet can be accepted** (an alternative returns 422). A better
42	   alternative is sent back as our sheet; it agrees and becomes standing (P10).
43	8. **Raw-material distributors refuse a fixed price beyond 12 months and refuse any deadband**
44	   (P08, P18): take their clause and negotiate the price; insisting on a deadband stalled them.
45	   But only when their sheet with the clause costs us less than their last one: Nordmark's copper
46	   clause came alone and cost 1.8 % of spend, score 0 (P02 `680eb11405186b42`,
47	   `d52ccdd3d2e07b3f`). That rule separates all 24 P02, P08 and P18 sessions correctly.
48	9. **RFQ: the arena answers one call per session at a time** and each thread's 60 s clock runs
49	   from its reply, so sends are serialized by deadline; the cheapest rival offer is a new,
50	   verified claim to every other bidder every round (P05 0.83, D02 0.73).
51	10. **The ceiling is lower than 0.9.** Best per case over all teams averages 0.82 (`/v1/live`,
52	    Saturday evening); practice C_best for P04 needs 4.93 against a frozen 4.94.

72	## Score and terms
73	
74	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **The category goal sets the rates of C**, not the case type (P13 is a price
75	  increase under `leverage`, P06 an RFQ under `stabilise`). From all 21 case files:
76	
77	  | Goal | Fallback risk | Relationship charge | Push for |
78	  |---|---|---|---|
79	  | `leverage` | 3 % (D02: 5 %) | no | price: rival quotes, should-cost, indices |
80	  | `routine` | 5 % | no | price and a quick close; small stakes |
81	  | `quality_first` | 8 % | no | low `ppm_commitment`, chargeback at least `cost_per_defect` |
82	  | `stabilise` | 10 % | yes, sustainable margin 0.5 to 8 % | structure: term, start date, payment, fair clause |
83	  | `secure_supply` | 25 % | yes, 4 to 10 % | full coverage and lead time first, then price |
84	
85	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Every session reveals C_best, also a walk-away**, plus our cost breakdown
86	  computed with the supplier's true numbers, relationship charge included. D01 walk-away after
87	  one message: c_open 448,810.67, c_best 408,623.99. → One session per case gives its target,
88	  and a relationship charge gives the supplier's true margin, i.e. its full cost.
89	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Uncovered need** costs `fallback_unit_price` plus `fallback_risk_pct` % of
90	  it; coverage is `min(volume, need) x min(months / 12, horizon)`. Committed volume above the need
91	  is bought anyway; months beyond the horizon neither cost nor earn. Evidence and examples:
92	  takeaway 2.
93	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Index clause** cost: `spend x material_share x (|path| - deadband)`, signed
94	  like the case's `index_paths`, plus `index_risk_pct` % of `spend x material_share` whenever a
95	  clause exists. Only a falling path larger than the risk charge makes a clause pay.
96	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Late delivery** is `late_cost_per_day x days beyond need_lead_time_days`,
97	  one sum per case. Must-haves can cap the lead time (P05: at most 42 days).
98	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Effective date:** units bought before it cost the current price, so a
99	  later start is worth months x volume x price step. Negotiable in D01, P01, P13. D01 at 50.90
100	  and 24 months: April instead of December start, 0.73 to 0.81; plus 60-day payment, 0.87.
101	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Our money:** 8 % a year and reference 60 days in all 21 cases. Paying 30
102	  days earlier costs 0.67 % of spend.
103	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Relationship charge** (`stabilise`, `secure_supply`) grows with the square
104	  of the first 5 missing margin points, so the cheapest deal sits below the sustainable margin
105	  (D01: about 2 points below its 4 %) unless the supplier's cost floor binds first. It also
106	  moves with payment terms: P02 carried 5,483 at 368.70 and 90 days, 901 at 366.41 and 14 days.

import copy

def sim_url():

and a bundle without a should-cost. Fake tables, no network, no model."""

import copy
import time

import pytest
from arena_kit import complete_offer
from arena_kit.client import ArenaError
from arena_kit.sim import load_cases

from buyer import economics as eco
from buyer import llm, runner

def s01(price=15.0):
    case = copy.deepcopy(load_cases()["case:S01"])
    return case, complete_offer(case, {"unit_price": price, "payment_days": 60})


def offer(sheet_id, terms, status="offer"):
    return {
        "from": "supplier",
        "status": status,
        "body": "Our offer.",
        "term_sheets": [{"term_sheet_id": sheet_id, "terms": terms}],
    }


def action(decision):
    return decision["message"]["action"]


def test_close_walks_when_the_alternative_is_cheaper():
    case, terms = s01(15.0)
    case["buyer"]["alternative"] = {
        "kind": "rfq",
        "terms": complete_offer(case, {"unit_price": 14.0, "payment_days": 60}),
    }
    neg = Negotiator(case)
    assert action(neg.close({"sup:a": [offer("ts1", terms)]})) == {"type": "walk_away"}
    cheaper = {**terms, "unit_price": 13.0}
    assert action(neg.close({"sup:a": [offer("ts2", cheaper)]})) == {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "ts2"}


def test_relationship_charge_reverses_the_accept():
    case, terms = s01(15.0)
    b = case["buyer"]
    b.update(category_goal="stabilise", relationship_eur_per_point=2000, sustainable_margin_pct=15)
    b["alternative"] = {"kind": "rfq", "terms": complete_offer(case, {"unit_price": 15.2, "payment_days": 60})}
    neg = Negotiator(case)
    threads = {"sup:a": [offer("ts1", terms)]}
    assert action(neg.close(threads))["type"] == "accept"  # no full-cost estimate: no charge
    neg.sides["sup:a"] = side = Side("sup:a")
    side.est = eco.estimate(case, {}, 0.08, full_cost=14.9)  # a margin far below 15 %
    assert eco.deal_cost(case, terms, {}) is not None
    assert eco.deal_cost(case, terms, {}, side.est) is None
    assert action(neg.close(threads)) == {"type": "walk_away"}


def test_broken_sheets_are_skipped_not_fatal():

class FakeTable:
    session_id = "fake"

    def __init__(self, case, threads, send=None, close=None, missed=None):
        self.case, self.threads = case, threads
        self._send, self._close, self._missed = send, close, missed
        self.closed = []

    def open(self, case_id):
        return self.case, self.threads

    def attachment(self, attachment_id):
        raise AssertionError("no attachments")

    def send(self, sid, message):
        return self._send(sid, message)

    def close(self, sid, message):
        self.closed.append((sid, message))
        return self._close(sid, message)

    def missed(self, sid, error):
        return self._missed(sid, error)

def test_a_refused_close_decides_again_with_the_guards():

"""What the supplier's e-mail asks of us. The bots write their asks in a few fixed sentences
("Which volume can you commit to?", "Please send us the data.", "Faster payment would help us
more than anything"), so plain patterns read them; no model, no latency."""

import re

ASKS = {
    # a binding volume figure; stated in words with the figure, it was "taken into account" (D01, D02)
    "volume": r"volume (can )?you (can )?commit|binding (higher )?volume|higher (order )?volume|volume figures"
    r"|confirm .{0,40}volume|anticipated (order )?volume",
    # proof of the forecast or of figures we mentioned without an ID
    "proof": r"proof of|send us the data|figures is that based|provide the (volume|forecast|binding)"
    r"|forecast data|volume data",
    # it wants to be paid sooner
    "payment": r"faster payment|pay(ment)? (terms )?(earlier|faster|sooner|within)|need .{0,12}days payment"
    r"|shorter payment|quicker payment|cash flow",
    # it asks for our current price level or our target
    "target": r"what price|which price|your target|price you have in mind",
}


def asks(body):
    """The kinds of ask in a supplier e-mail, in a fixed order."""
    text = body or ""
    return [k for k, pat in ASKS.items() if re.search(pat, text, re.I)]

"""The published cost function: what a term sheet costs the buyer in €, plus term helpers.

C covers the buyer's fixed need over a fixed horizon: need the deal does not cover is bought at
the case's fallback price (plus the fallback risk of the category goal), committed volume is bought
needed or not, and units bought before a new price takes effect cost the current price. In
strategic and bottleneck cases a deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin costs
too - pass your estimate of the supplier (`supplier_value`) to price that. Do the arithmetic here,
not in the language model.
"""

import math
import operator
from datetime import date

# Strategic and bottleneck goals: leaving the supplier below a sustainable margin costs.
RELATIONSHIP_GOALS = {"stabilise", "secure_supply"}
OPS = {
    "<=": operator.le,
    "<": operator.lt,
    ">=": operator.ge,
    ">": operator.gt,
    "==": operator.eq,
    "!=": operator.ne,
}


def closing_terms(case, terms, standard=None):
    """The terms a deal would close on: the term sheet, then the supplier's standard terms (from
    its quote PDF) for anything left out, then the case's fixed terms; gaps from the buyer's plan.
    """
    b = case["buyer"]
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan = {
        "volume_per_year": b["need_per_year"],
        "contract_months": round(12 * b["horizon_years"]),
        "payment_days": b["reference_payment_days"],
        "lead_time_days": b["need_lead_time_days"],
        # an unknown Incoterm counts as the costliest: a cautious buyer does not assume DAP
        "incoterm": max(freight, key=freight.get),
    }
    t = dict(plan)
    for layer in (standard or {}, case.get("fixed_terms", {}), terms):
        t.update({k: v for k, v in layer.items() if v is not None or k not in plan})
    return t


def horizon_start(case):
    """The horizon starts at the fixed or the earliest possible effective date."""
    fixed = case.get("fixed_terms", {}).get("effective_date")
    options = [o for o in case.get("term_options", {}).get("effective_date", []) if o]
    first = fixed or (min(options) if options else None)
    return date.fromisoformat(first) if first else None


def _years(case, t):
    """Years of the horizon a deal covers; a single order (0 months) counts as one year's lot.
    A commitment beyond the horizon neither costs nor earns."""
    months = t["contract_months"]
    return min(months / 12 if months else 1.0, case["buyer"]["horizon_years"])


def _units_before(case, t, years):
    """Units bought between the horizon start and the date a new price takes effect."""
    start = horizon_start(case)
    if not t.get("effective_date") or start is None:
        return 0.0
    lag = (date.fromisoformat(t["effective_date"]) - start).days / 365
    return t["volume_per_year"] * min(max(lag, 0.0), years)


def supplier_value(case, terms, supplier):
    """What a deal is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash: the price at its standard terms that
    would pay it the same. `supplier` is your estimate of it:
      standard       its standard terms (quote PDF, `docs.standard_terms`)
      interest_rate  what money now is worth to it per year (more to a supplier short of cash)
      usual_rate     its usual cost of money (default: interest_rate); tooling paid up front is
                     worth more to it when cash is dearer than usual
      ppm            the defect rate it really achieves (default: its standard ppm commitment)
      extra          EUR per unit it gains (+) or spends (-) beyond these items, e.g. overtime for
                     a faster delivery or idle capacity a larger volume fills (default 0)
    Contract length and an index clause are security, not cash: they do not count here."""
    b, std = case["buyer"], {**supplier["standard"], **case.get("fixed_terms", {})}
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, std)
    years = _years(case, t)
    sold = t["volume_per_year"] * years
    old = _units_before(case, t, years) / sold  # sold at the current price
    rate = supplier["interest_rate"]
    pay = 1 - rate * (t["payment_days"] - std["payment_days"]) / 360
    cash_now = 1 + (rate - supplier.get("usual_rate", rate)) * years / 2
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    ppm = supplier.get("ppm", std.get("ppm_commitment") or 0)
    return (
        t["unit_price"] * (1 - old) * pay
        + old * (b.get("current_unit_price") or 0.0) * pay
        + freight[t["incoterm"]]
        - freight[std["incoterm"]]  # it carries the freight leg
        + ((t.get("tooling_eur") or 0) - (std.get("tooling_eur") or 0)) / sold * cash_now
        - ppm / 1e6 * ((t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0) - (std.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0))
        + supplier.get("extra", 0.0)
    )


def _soft(gap):
    """Margin points below the sustainable margin, as they cost: none above it, quadratic over
    the first 5 points, linear beyond - no kink."""
    if gap <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return gap * gap / 10 if gap <= 5 else gap - 2.5


def relationship_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None, value=None):
    """Strategic and bottleneck goals only: EUR for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier
    below `sustainable_margin_pct`, per year covered. `supplier["full_cost"]` (EUR per unit) is your
    estimate of its full cost; `value` overrides `supplier_value`. Without an estimate: 0."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    per_point, sustainable = b.get("relationship_eur_per_point"), b.get("sustainable_margin_pct")
    if b.get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not per_point or not sustainable or not supplier:
        return 0.0
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    worth = value if value is not None else supplier_value(case, t, supplier)
    margin = (worth - supplier["full_cost"]) / worth * 100
    return per_point * _soft(sustainable - margin) * _years(case, t)


def cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C by part. `standard`: the supplier's standard terms for anything the term sheet leaves out.
    `supplier`: your estimate of the supplier for the relationship term (`supplier_value`)."""
    b, t = case["buyer"], closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    if t.get("unit_price") is None:
        raise ValueError("no unit_price: a term sheet without a price has no cost")
    years = _years(case, t)
    committed = t["volume_per_year"] * years  # bought, needed or not
    covered = min(t["volume_per_year"], b["need_per_year"]) * years
    pre = _units_before(case, t, years)
    at_new_price = (committed - pre) * t["unit_price"]
    spend = pre * (b.get("current_unit_price") or t["unit_price"]) + at_new_price
    per_defect = b.get("cost_per_defect", 0)
    defect_cost = per_defect - min(t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0, per_defect)
    index = index_risk = 0.0
    if clause := t.get("index_clause"):
        path = b.get("index_paths", {}).get(clause["series"], 0.0)
        moved = max(0.0, abs(path) - clause["deadband_pct"] / 100)
        index = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * moved * math.copysign(1, path)
        index_risk = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * b.get("index_risk_pct", 0) / 100
    uncovered = (b["need_per_year"] * b["horizon_years"] - covered) * b["fallback_unit_price"]
    need = b["need_lead_time_days"]
    return {
        "price": spend,
        "uncovered_need": uncovered,
        "fallback_risk": uncovered * b.get("fallback_risk_pct", 0) / 100,
        "payment_terms": spend * b["interest_rate"] * (b["reference_payment_days"] - t["payment_days"]) / 360,
        "freight": committed * b["freight_eur_per_unit"][t["incoterm"]],
        "late_delivery": b.get("late_cost_per_day", 0) * max(0, t["lead_time_days"] - need),
        "quality": committed * (t.get("ppm_commitment") or 0) / 1e6 * defect_cost,
        "tooling": t.get("tooling_eur") or 0.0,
        "index_clause": index,
        "index_risk": index_risk,
        "relationship": relationship_cost(case, t, supplier=supplier),
    }


def total_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C in EUR; infinite for terms without a price (e.g. a supplier that quotes none), so such a
    sheet is never the cheapest and never beats an alternative."""
    if closing_terms(case, terms, standard).get("unit_price") is None:
        return math.inf
    return round(sum(cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard, supplier).values()), 2)


def score(c_open, c_deal, c_best):
    if c_deal is None:
        return 0.0
    if c_open - c_best <= 0.01:  # no room to negotiate: matching the best is full marks
        return 1.0 if c_deal <= c_best + 0.01 else 0.0
    return min(1.0, max(0.0, (c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)))


def must_haves_ok(case, terms, standard=None):
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    for m in case["buyer"].get("must_haves", []):
        value = t.get(m["field"])
        if value is None and m["op"] not in ("==", "!="):
            return False
        if not OPS[m["op"]](value, m["value"]):
            return False
    return True


def snap(case, field, value):
    """The allowed value closest to `value` (case `term_options`), else `value` unchanged."""
    options = case.get("term_options", {}).get(field)
    if not options or value in options:
        return value
    if isinstance(value, int | float) and all(isinstance(o, int | float) for o in options):
        return min(options, key=lambda o: (abs(o - value), o))
    return options[0]


def complete_offer(case, terms):
    """A valid term sheet: exactly the negotiable fields, gaps from the buyer's plan, snapped."""

## Policies
- Standard payment terms: 60 days net. Cost of capital for valuing payment terms:
  8% a year.
- Approval: deals above EUR 250 k a year need the head of purchasing, above EUR 1 M the managing director.
- A-parts are dual-sourced where a qualified second source exists (`sourcing.csv`).
- Quality agreement with every series supplier: on-time delivery target 95 %, flat fee of
  EUR 150 per supplier-caused complaint, 8D report within 60 days.
- Preferred Incoterm: DAP Hollerau. Freight for EXW/FCA deliveries is booked by Hollerau.

## Should-cost
`should_cost.csv` estimates full cost without margin. For the parts of strategic and bottleneck
negotiations the category team modelled the current supplier's own plant (`supplier_id`, error about
5 %); the other rows use a German cost base with an error of 5-15 %. Rule of thumb for other countries'
full cost relative to Germany: AT and CH about 1.0-1.1, CZ, PL and HU about 0.8-0.85, TR about 0.75,
CN about 0.7.

## Category strategies
Every negotiation states its category goal (`stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage`, `routine`); the rates of its cost C follow it.
Quality escalations are `quality_first`, capacity squeezes `secure_supply`, kits and bundles `routine`.

| Category | Strategy | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| castings | secure supply and energy-cost transparency; build Central-European second sources | stabilise |
| machined parts | leverage: competition between local job shops, bundle small parts | leverage |
| sheet metal | leverage; quality first after the 2026 base-frame issues | leverage |
| seals | bottleneck: long-term agreements, qualify second sources where approvals allow | secure_supply |
| electrical | strategic: copper and electronics clauses, multi-year frameworks | stabilise |
| C-parts | routine: fewer suppliers, kits, lower process cost | routine |
| raw material | index-based pricing, negotiate base price and extras | leverage |

## Targets for FY2027
Material cost -3 % against the index-adjusted baseline; no supplier in red for more than two quarters.
**For us.** Useful as a secondary signal, not a stop rule: the bot stops on patience before its
floor, so a floor estimate mostly tells us whether a relationship charge is near (stabilise,
secure supply) and whether a large first concession means room (already `DEEP` in the policy).
The relationship charge in a finished practice result gives the supplier's true margin and cost
(`learnings.md`), which beats any curve fit for practice cases.

## 7. Procurement levers by supplier situation

**Research** (practice literature: Kraljic 1983, consultancy and CIPS sources; conventions, not
studies): classify the position first (leverage: compete and push price; bottleneck and strategic:
secure supply and joint value); answer a price-increase letter with a line-item breakdown weighted
by each driver's cost share; accept justified increases only index-linked or temporary; price
payment terms at both sides' cost of money; index clauses with a deadband of 3 to 5 %, a lag,
a cap, both directions and only the exposed cost share; threaten a second source only if it is
real; agree chargebacks before the dispute. Preferred-customer research (Schiele et al.): suppliers
reward attractive customers with capacity and price; forecast visibility and payment reliability
are what they ask for most. Collaborative but assertive buyers realise more value (Vantage
Partners survey, correlational).

**Playbook**, joined with our persona signals (`learnings.md`, Persona signals):

| Situation | Signal in the data | Give | Ask | Avoid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cash short | "bank is watching", "pay earlier", cash discount | faster payment when its rate beats our 8 % (cash discounts imply 37 to 56 %/yr) | price | ignoring its ask when payment is fixed: say so and offer the next best currency |
| Fully booked | "fully booked", "allocates volumes" | its lead time, a firm 24-month volume, forecast | price at its standard speed | deep anchors (P10 patience 0.015), paying overtime for speed we do not value |
| Spare capacity | "second shift on hold" | volume, extra parts, long term | price | |
| Price frozen | "no room on price", "price list applies to all" | nothing on price | payment days, contract length, freight, start date | price pushes (no move, only lost patience) |
| Approval ladder | "above 2 % need the approval" | small steps (2 % or less), a reason the rep can forward to its boss | | one big ask that goes to a committee |
| Index-driven distributor | material share in its quote, clause offered | contract length only with a clause we can live with | deadband, share limited to material, falling series only | taking a 0 % deadband clause on a rising series (P02: score 0) |
| Price increase letter | letter above its drivers' index move | the index-weighted justified part, later start | notice period, start date, split | citing indices that rose (they confirm its case) |
| Stabilise, near cost | own-plant should-cost close to the quote | the price with the lowest C incl. relationship charge | terms | squeezing below sustainable margin (charge grows with the square) |
# docs

Ours:

- `learnings.md`: what we know about the arena, its suppliers and the data package, with evidence.
- `design.md`: the agent we are building. `how-it-works.pdf` holds its architecture diagram.
- `negotiation-research.md`: negotiation strategies from the literature, checked against our traces, with an experiment plan.

Tacto's, copied from [tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit](https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit)

- `challenge.md`: the participant brief (story, task, score, rules, timeline)
- `api.md`: the HTTP API, message format, claim checks, the cost function C
- `submission.md`: what to hand in on ehl.gg by Sunday 12:00, and the pitch
# Generalisation to the Live Final

How well the agent on `steffen/price-engine` (commit `9182604`) should carry over to Sunday: new
suppliers, up to a third of cases mixing supplier and case types practice never showed, some
citing the 08:00 release. Research on Saturday 10 October, evening: the kit's code, all 21 case
files, `logs/runs/`, `exports/`, the data package, and our agent on `arena-sim`. No practice
quota spent. Same conventions as `learnings.md`: date, tag, finding, evidence, consequence.

## Verdict

The code runs on every case structure we know. Its tuning is in-sample and unmeasured beyond
the ten hosted cases. The biggest gaps for Sunday: new suppliers get a neutral profile because
the release's letters and news never reach the persona code; one exception loses a whole case
(or every later wave); four or more bidders time out.

| # | Risk | Damage | Fix | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | an exception in a move or the wave poll | a case at its alternative (0 in 6 of 21), or all later waves | catch per move, keep polling | small |
| 2 | release rows invisible to SQL; most suppliers without text | neutral profile for new suppliers | read release rows via the ID index; scan the supplier's e-mails | small to medium |
| 3 | 4 or more bidders | timeouts, lost patience, ended threads | stop sending to the worst bidders after round 1 | medium, a tactics decision |
| 4 | missed phrasings in `SIGNALS` | traits not detected | widen to word stems | small |
| 5 | `price_unit` ignored | wrong-direction rival or order-price claims | divide by `price_unit` | small |

## Findings

- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Every known case structure runs end to end.** All 21 public case files,
  including the nine never hosted (P06, P09, P12 to P17, P19), played through `arena-sim`

  bundles (P07 4 parts, P15 3), the 3-bidder RFQ, `tooling_eur` (P06) and up to 75 term
  combinations (P09). The sim's supplier is a fixed script, so this checks code paths, not
  tactics. → Worth a test in `tests/` that plays every case file from `GET /v1/cases` this way
  (load them into `Sim(cases, pkg.facts)`, strip the `hosted` key).
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **One exception loses a case.** `play_case` has no guard around

  `unit_price` (`claims.py` `rival_quote`), an index clause without `material_share`

"""The preparation agent: the model reads the case briefing and looks things up in the data
package itself (SQL, ID lookup, documents) before the session opens, then proposes a stance per
supplier: what it values, which arguments to lead with, how much of the room to capture, how deep
to open, how much patience to show, the tone, and an assessment in words for the e-mails.

Code clamps every figure to a band around the computed plan (`briefing.plan`) and goes on with the
plan alone when the model is late, broken or silent. The loop runs before the session opens, so no
supplier clock is running; it still has a hard wall-clock budget because the wave's cap is."""

import json
import logging
import re
import time

from . import llm

log = logging.getLogger("buyer")
BUDGET_S = 25.0  # wall clock for the whole loop per case
STEP_S = 12.0  # one model answer
MAX_STEPS = 6  # lookups before the stance is due
MAX_ROWS = 25
BANDS = {"capture_delta": (-0.15, 0.15), "opening_gap_delta": (-0.05, 0.08), "patience": (0.15, 1.0)}
CLAIM_KINDS = ("should_cost", "order_history", "index", "rival", "notice", "forecast", "scorecard", "hedged", "open_book")
TOOLS_RE = re.compile(r"\{.*\}", re.S)

SYSTEM = """You are the preparation analyst of the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a German
pump maker. A buyer agent is about to negotiate the case below by e-mail with the suppliers listed.
Your job: read the briefing, look up what matters in our data package, and hand the buyer a stance
per supplier.

Answer every turn with exactly ONE JSON object and nothing else:
- {"query": "SELECT ..."}      one read-only SQL statement over the package (tables below, at most
                                 25 rows come back)
- {"lookup": "<id>"}           the fact behind a citable ID (doc:, news:, ctr:, quote:, sc:, cost:, ...)
- {"document": "<id>"}         the text of a letter, call note or news item
- {"stance": {"<supplier_id>": {...}, ...}}   your final answer, one entry per supplier

A stance entry:
  "assessment": 2 to 3 sentences in words for the person writing the e-mails: who this supplier is
                to us, what it values, what to acknowledge. No figures, no IDs.
  "values": what it wants from us, from the data (e.g. "faster payment", "a firm volume",
            "a long contract", "its lead time", "planning security"), 1 to 4 items
  "lead_with": the kinds of argument to use first, from: should_cost, order_history, index, rival,
               notice, forecast, scorecard, hedged, open_book
  "capture_delta": -0.15 to 0.15, how much more (+) or less (-) of the possible saving to go for
                   than the plan: + when the data shows it usually moves or has spare capacity,
                   - when it is frozen, fully booked, selling near cost or walks away easily
  "opening_gap_delta": -0.05 to 0.08, how much deeper (+) or shallower (-) to open than the plan
  "patience": 0.15 to 1.0, the cumulative gap it will tolerate (low for touchy suppliers)
  "tone": "warm" or "firm"
  "risks": up to 3 short items

Use at most a few lookups: its letters and call notes, its scorecard, our payment behaviour, its
negotiation record, other quotes for the part. Then answer with the stance. Be quick."""


def tools_text(pkg):
    if pkg is None:
        return "No data package: answer with the stance right away."
    try:
        tables = pkg.tables()
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - no SQLite
        return "The package has no SQL tables; use lookup and document only."
    return "TABLES:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {t}: {', '.join(c.split()[0] for c in m['columns'])}" for t, m in tables.items())


def case_text(case, brief):
    b = case["buyer"]
    econ = brief.get("economics") or {}
    cons = brief.get("constraints") or {}
    lines = [
        f"CASE {case['case_id']}: {case.get('title')}",
        f"BRIEFING: {case.get('briefing')}",
        f"TYPE {case.get('type')}, GOAL {b.get('category_goal')}, SUPPLIERS {', '.join(case.get('suppliers') or [])}",
        f"PARTS {', '.join(case.get('parts') or [])}",
        f"NEGOTIABLE {cons.get('negotiable')}; OPTIONS {json.dumps(cons.get('options'))}",
        f"FIXED {json.dumps(cons.get('fixed'))}; MUST-HAVES {json.dumps(cons.get('must_haves'))}",
        f"NEED {econ.get('need_per_year')} a year over {econ.get('horizon_years')} years; current price "
        f"{econ.get('current_unit_price')}; fallback price {econ.get('fallback_unit_price')}; "
        f"alternative {econ.get('alternative')}; C of the alternative {econ.get('c_alt')}",
        f"REFS {', '.join(case.get('refs') or [])}",
    ]
    for part, m in (brief.get("market") or {}).items():
        lines.append(f"MARKET {part}: quotes {json.dumps(m.get('quotes'))[:600]}")
        lines.append(f"  prices {json.dumps(m.get('prices'))[:400]}")
        lines.append(f"  should-cost {json.dumps(m.get('should_cost'))[:400]}")
        lines.append(f"  drivers {json.dumps(m.get('drivers'))[:400]}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def execute(pkg, call):
    """One tool call of the model, as text for the next turn. Read-only by construction."""
    if pkg is None:
        return "no data package"
    try:
        if "query" in call:
            rows = pkg.query(str(call["query"]), (), MAX_ROWS)
            return json.dumps(rows, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)[:4000]
        if "lookup" in call:
            return json.dumps(pkg.lookup(str(call["lookup"])), ensure_ascii=False, default=str)[:2000]
        if "document" in call:
            return pkg.document(str(call["document"]))[:3000]
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - a bad SQL statement is the model's problem, not the move's
        return f"error: {e}"
    return "unknown call: answer with query, lookup, document or stance"


def parse(text):
    m = TOOLS_RE.search(text or "")
    if not m:
        return None
    try:
        return json.loads(m.group(0))
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return None


def clamp(stance, suppliers):
    """Only known suppliers, every figure inside its band, every list of known words."""
    out = {}
    for sid in suppliers:
        s = stance.get(sid) if isinstance(stance, dict) else None
        if not isinstance(s, dict):
            continue
        c = {"assessment": " ".join(str(s.get("assessment") or "").split())[:600]}
        for k, (lo, hi) in BANDS.items():
            try:
                c[k] = round(min(hi, max(lo, float(s[k]))), 3)
            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
                pass
        c["values"] = [str(v)[:60] for v in (s.get("values") or []) if v][:4]
        c["lead_with"] = [k for k in (s.get("lead_with") or []) if k in CLAIM_KINDS][:4]
        c["risks"] = [str(v)[:80] for v in (s.get("risks") or []) if v][:3]
        c["tone"] = s.get("tone") if s.get("tone") in ("warm", "firm") else None
        if llm.FORBIDDEN.search(c["assessment"]):
            c["assessment"] = ""  # figures or leaks: the e-mails do without it
        out[sid] = c
    return out


def run(complete, case, pkg, brief, budget_s=BUDGET_S):
    """{supplier_id: stance} from the model's loop, or {} without a model, on a timeout or on
    anything unexpected. Never raises."""
    if complete is None:
        return {}
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    transcript = [case_text(case, brief), tools_text(pkg), "Answer with your first JSON object."]
    steps = []
    try:
        for _ in range(MAX_STEPS + 1):
            left = budget_s - (time.monotonic() - t0)
            if left < llm.MIN_S:
                break
            text = llm.POOL.submit(complete, SYSTEM, "\n\n".join(transcript)).result(timeout=min(STEP_S, left))
            call = parse(text)
            if call is None:
                transcript.append("Your last answer was not one JSON object. Answer with the stance now.")
                continue
            if "stance" in call:
                stance = clamp(call["stance"], case.get("suppliers") or [])
                log.info("%s prep: stance for %s in %.1fs after %d lookups", case["case_id"], list(stance), time.monotonic() - t0, len(steps))
                return {"stance": stance, "steps": steps, "took_s": round(time.monotonic() - t0, 1)}
            result = execute(pkg, call)
            steps.append({"call": call, "result": result[:300]})
            transcript += [f"YOU: {json.dumps(call)}", f"RESULT: {result}"]
            if len(steps) >= MAX_STEPS:
                transcript.append("No more lookups: answer with the stance now.")
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - a slow or broken model must not cost the case
        log.warning("%s prep: no stance after %.1fs: %s", case["case_id"], time.monotonic() - t0, e)
    return {"stance": {}, "steps": steps, "took_s": round(time.monotonic() - t0, 1)}

    one round of each open thread takes, since the threads are served one message at a time.

"""Pacing by the wave's clock: the share of the gap grows when the clock leaves fewer rounds than
the round limit; the runner derives the rounds from the cap, the measured round time and the open
threads; a capped case closes before the cap. No network, no model."""

import copy
import time

import pytest
from arena_kit import complete_offer
from arena_kit.sim import load_cases

from buyer import runner
from buyer.policy import FRACTION, MAX_FRACTION, Negotiator, pace


def test_pace_grows_as_the_clock_tightens():
    assert pace(9, 9) == FRACTION
    assert pace(9, 12) == FRACTION  # more rounds on the clock than the limit allows: the plain path
    assert pace(9, 0) == FRACTION  # no information: the plain path
    assert FRACTION < pace(9, 6) < pace(9, 4) <= MAX_FRACTION
    assert pace(9, 3) == MAX_FRACTION
    assert pace(9, 1) == MAX_FRACTION
    # the paced path ends where the plain path would have after `left` rounds
    assert (1 - pace(9, 6)) ** 6 == pytest.approx((1 - FRACTION) ** 9)


def test_rounds_by_clock():
    assert runner.rounds_by_clock(None, 0.0, 25, 3) is None
    # 480 s cap, 90 s close margin, 30 s rounds, 3 open threads: 390 / 90 = 4.33 rounds each
    assert runner.rounds_by_clock(480.0, 0.0, 30, 3) == pytest.approx(390 / 90)
    assert runner.rounds_by_clock(480.0, 0.0, 30, 1) == pytest.approx(13)
    assert runner.rounds_by_clock(100.0, 50.0, 30, 2) == 0.0  # inside the close margin


def offer(sheet_id, terms, status="open"):
    return {"from": "supplier", "status": status, "body": "Our offer.", "term_sheets": [{"term_sheet_id": sheet_id, "terms": terms}]}


def test_a_tight_clock_moves_further_in_a_round():
    case = copy.deepcopy(load_cases()["case:S01"])
    sid = case["suppliers"][0]
    quote = complete_offer(case, {"unit_price": 15.0, "payment_days": 60})

    def price_after_round_two(rounds):
        neg = Negotiator(case)
        threads = {sid: [offer("o1", quote)]}
        first = neg.move(sid, threads, rounds=rounds)["message"]
        threads[sid] += [{**first, "from": "buyer"}, offer("o2", {**quote, "unit_price": 14.5})]
        second = neg.move(sid, threads, rounds=rounds)["message"]
        return first["term_sheets"][0]["terms"]["unit_price"], second["term_sheets"][0]["terms"]["unit_price"]

    a1, relaxed = price_after_round_two(None)
    b1, tight = price_after_round_two(2)
    assert a1 == b1  # the anchor does not depend on the clock
    assert tight > relaxed  # with two rounds left we move more of the gap
    assert tight < 14.5  # and stay below its counter


class SlowTable:
    """A supplier that answers at once; the wall clock is faked by the test."""

    session_id = "fake"

    def __init__(self, case, quote):
        self.case, self.quote, self.sent, self.closed = case, quote, 0, None

    def open(self, case_id):
        sid = self.case["suppliers"][0]
        return self.case, {sid: [offer("o0", self.quote)]}

    def send(self, sid, message):
        self.sent += 1
        price = round(self.quote["unit_price"] - 0.1 * self.sent, 2)
        return offer(f"o{self.sent}", {**self.quote, "unit_price": price})

    def close(self, sid, message):
        self.closed = message
        return {"deal": True, "terms": self.quote, "c_open": 1.0, "c_deal": 1.0, "c_best": 1.0, "score": 1.0}


def test_a_capped_case_closes_before_the_cap(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Each round takes 40 s of (faked) wall clock; with a 300 s cap and a 90 s close margin the
    runner sends at most five messages, then accepts the standing sheet."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, "RUNS", tmp_path)
    case = copy.deepcopy(load_cases()["case:S01"])
    quote = complete_offer(case, {"unit_price": 15.0, "payment_days": 60})
    table = SlowTable(case, quote)
    clock = {"t": 1000.0}
    monkeypatch.setattr(time, "time", lambda: clock["t"])
    monkeypatch.setattr(time, "monotonic", lambda: clock["t"])
    real_send = table.send

    def slow_send(sid, message):
        clock["t"] += 40
        return real_send(sid, message)

    table.send = slow_send
    result = runner.play_case(table, case["case_id"], deadline=1000.0 + 300)
    assert result["deal"]
    assert table.closed["action"]["type"] == "accept"
    assert table.sent <= 5  # (300 - 90) / 40

"""The preparation agent's briefing and plan: importance tiers, the C floor, the capture target,
the opening bounds; the stance clamped; the plan built for every case file. The package tests run
only where `data/package` is unpacked (gitignored)."""

import copy
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from arena_kit import complete_offer
from arena_kit.sim import load_cases

from buyer import briefing, prep
from buyer.agent import load_package
from buyer.policy import Negotiator

PACKAGE = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "data" / "package"
CASES = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "logs" / "cases"


def offer(terms, status="open"):
    return [{"from": "supplier", "status": status, "body": "Our offer.", "term_sheets": [{"term_sheet_id": "o1", "terms": terms}]}]


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def pkg():
    if not (PACKAGE / "facts.json").is_file():
        pytest.skip("no data package")
    return load_package(str(PACKAGE))


def practice(case_id):
    for case in json.loads((CASES / "practice.json").read_text()):
        if case["case_id"] == case_id:
            return {k: v for k, v in case.items() if k != "hosted"}
    raise KeyError(case_id)


def test_importance_without_a_package_is_standard():
    case = copy.deepcopy(load_cases()["case:S01"])
    assert briefing.importance(None, case, case["suppliers"][0])["tier"] == "standard"
    case["buyer"]["alternative"] = None
    assert briefing.importance(None, case, case["suppliers"][0])["why"] == ["no fallback in this case"]


def test_importance_tiers_from_the_package(pkg):
    strategic = briefing.importance(pkg, practice("case:P02"), "sup:70510")  # sole source, A, 9 % of spend
    assert strategic["tier"] == "strategic"
    assert "our only active source for this part" in strategic["why"]
    assert briefing.importance(pkg, practice("case:P07"), "sup:70610")["tier"] == "standard"  # 40 % of a C-part
    assert briefing.importance(pkg, practice("case:P08"), "sup:70710")["tier"] == "important"


def test_plan_on_every_case_file(pkg):
    """Every case file (hosted or not) gets a plan with a floor, a C floor and opening bounds."""
    for path in sorted(CASES.glob("*.json")):
        for case in json.loads(path.read_text()):
            case = {k: v for k, v in case.items() if k != "hosted"}
            current = case["buyer"].get("current_unit_price") or case["buyer"]["fallback_unit_price"]
            quote = complete_offer(case, {"unit_price": round(current * 1.1, 2)})
            for sid in case["suppliers"]:
                neg = Negotiator(case, pkg)
                s = neg.setup(sid, offer(quote))
                p = s.plan
                assert p["importance"]["tier"] in briefing.TIERS, case["case_id"]
                assert 0 < p["floor"] <= s.quote, case["case_id"]
                assert p["c_floor"] <= p["c_start"] + 1e-6 or not p["floor_binding"], case["case_id"]
                assert 0.4 <= p["capture"] <= 0.9
                assert p["opening_min"] <= s.anchor <= s.quote, case["case_id"]
                if p["opening_max"] is not None:
                    assert s.anchor <= p["opening_max"] + 0.01, case["case_id"]
                if s.target:
                    assert s.floor is None or s.target >= s.floor - 0.01
                    assert s.target < s.quote


def test_a_floor_near_its_quote_is_a_reference_not_a_bound(pkg):
    """Brandlhuber quotes below our should-cost plus margin: the floor stays off, the capture
    target too, and the opening is today's price plus half the justified increase."""
    case = practice("case:P01")
    quote = complete_offer(case, {"unit_price": 138.55, "effective_date": "2026-11-01", "payment_days": 30})
    s = Negotiator(case, pkg).setup("sup:70110", offer(quote))
    assert s.plan["importance"]["tier"] == "strategic"
    assert s.plan["cost_confidence"] == "high"
    assert not s.plan["floor_binding"]
    assert s.floor is None
    assert s.plan["justified"]["justified_pct"] < s.plan["justified"]["asked_pct"]
    assert s.anchor <= s.plan["opening_max"]


def test_a_binding_floor_bounds_the_sheet(pkg):
    """P10: an own-plant cost well below the quote binds; no sheet goes below it and the capture
    target sits between floor and quote."""
    case = practice("case:P10")
    quote = complete_offer(case, {"unit_price": 32.2, "volume_per_year": 19890, "contract_months": 12, "lead_time_days": 56})
    neg = Negotiator(case, pkg)
    s = neg.setup("sup:70410", offer(quote))
    assert s.plan["floor_binding"] and s.floor == s.plan["floor"]
    assert s.floor < s.target < s.quote * briefing.TARGET_BELOW_QUOTE
    s.ours.append(s.floor - 1.0)  # pretend we sat below the floor
    price, _ = neg.next_price(s, theirs=s.quote, left=9, rounds=9)
    assert price >= s.floor


def test_the_stance_is_clamped_and_applied(pkg):
    case = practice("case:P08")
    raw = {
        "sup:70710": {
            "assessment": "A distributor that prices off the alloy surcharge; acknowledge its index exposure.",
            "values": ["a long contract", 42, None],
            "lead_with": ["index", "nonsense", "should_cost"],
            "capture_delta": 0.9,
            "opening_gap_delta": -1,
            "patience": 0.05,
            "tone": "loud",
            "risks": ["final offer early"],
        },
        "sup:other": {"assessment": "ignored"},
    }
    stance = prep.clamp(raw, case["suppliers"])
    assert list(stance) == ["sup:70710"]
    st = stance["sup:70710"]
    assert st["capture_delta"] == 0.15 and st["opening_gap_delta"] == -0.05 and st["patience"] == 0.15
    assert st["values"] == ["a long contract", "42"] and st["lead_with"] == ["index", "should_cost"]
    assert st["tone"] is None
    quote = complete_offer(case, {"unit_price": 6.05, "payment_days": 30, "contract_months": 12, "index_clause": None})
    plain = Negotiator(case, pkg).setup("sup:70710", offer(quote))
    neg = Negotiator(case, pkg)
    neg.stance = stance
    s = neg.setup("sup:70710", offer(quote))
    assert s.budget == 0.15
    assert s.plan["capture"] == min(0.9, plain.plan["capture"] + 0.15)
    assert s.plan["opening_gap"] == pytest.approx(plain.plan["opening_gap"] - 0.05)
    assert [c["kind"] for c in s.claims][:1] == ["index"] or not any(c["kind"] == "index" for c in s.claims)
    digits = prep.clamp({"sup:70710": {"assessment": "We pay 30 days late."}}, case["suppliers"])
    assert digits["sup:70710"]["assessment"] == ""  # figures never reach the e-mail writer


def test_prep_loop_runs_lookups_then_takes_the_stance(pkg):
    case = practice("case:P02")
    brief = briefing.prepare(case, pkg, Negotiator(case, pkg).bank)
    answers = iter(
        [
            "not json at all",
            '{"query": "SELECT id FROM suppliers WHERE id = \'sup:70510\'"}',
            '{"document": "doc:nope"}',
            'Here you are: {"stance": {"sup:70510": {"assessment": "A group supplier with an approval ladder.", '
            '"values": ["planning security"], "lead_with": ["index"], "capture_delta": -0.1, "patience": 0.3, "tone": "firm"}}}',
        ]
    )
    seen = []

    def complete(system, user):
        seen.append(user)
        return next(answers)

    out = prep.run(complete, case, pkg, brief)
    assert list(out["stance"]) == ["sup:70510"]
    assert out["stance"]["sup:70510"]["capture_delta"] == -0.1
    assert len(out["steps"]) == 2
    assert "sup:70510" in out["steps"][0]["result"]
    assert out["steps"][1]["result"].startswith("error")
    assert "RESULT:" in seen[-1]  # the lookups' results reached the next turn


def test_prep_loop_gives_up_on_a_slow_model():
    case = copy.deepcopy(load_cases()["case:S01"])

    def slow(system, user):
        import time

        time.sleep(3)
        return '{"stance": {}}'

    out = prep.run(slow, case, None, {}, budget_s=2.5)
    assert out["stance"] == {}
    assert out["took_s"] < 3.5
    assert prep.run(None, case, None, {}) == {}

## Policy

A stance per supplier (opening gap, capture, margin, justified share, steps) proposed by the model
at case open, clamped by code to a range per tier and goal, logged with a reason. Fallback
constants when the stance call times out:

| Constant | Values |
|---|---|
| capture (share of possible saving before accepting) | leverage 0.75, quality_first 0.65, stabilise 0.6, secure_supply 0.55, routine 0.5 |
| opening gap below the quote (never below the floor) | strategic 5 %, important 8 %, standard 12 % |
| margin above full cost for the floor | case's `sustainable_margin_pct` in `stabilise` / `secure_supply`, else strategic 4 %, important 2 %, standard 0 % |
| justified share offered in round 1 of a price increase | strategic 0.5, important 0.25, standard 0 |
| concession steps, only after the supplier moved | 35, 25, 15, 10 % of the remaining gap |

Live signals adjust within bounds: approval needed shrinks steps (x0.7), high walk risk stops
price pushes. At the target, hold one more round while the supplier still moves.
input.new_string:
## Policy

Implemented in `buyer/briefing.py` (the variables) and `buyer/prep.py` (the model's stance): the
plan variables below are calculated per case and supplier from the data on every run, the model
proposes deltas within bands, and the run log assesses the C floor against the revealed C_best.

| Variable | Calculated from |
|---|---|
| full cost, confidence | own-plant should-cost (high), generic estimate scaled to the country (medium), else 80 % of the quote (low); a figure outside 0.3 to 1.3 of the quote is read per piece or dropped |
| floor price | full cost plus the case's sustainable margin (`stabilise`, `secure_supply`) or the tier margin (strategic 4 %, important 2 %, standard 0 %), as a price at our terms; binding only with a cost estimate and at most 95 % of the quote (P01, P02, P17 quote below our should-cost) |
| C floor | C of the cheapest allowed terms at the floor price: the reference for the run |
| capture | by goal (leverage 0.75, quality_first 0.65, stabilise 0.6, secure_supply 0.55, routine 0.5), +0.1 when its record shows it moves, -0.1 when frozen, booked or on an approval ladder, -0.15 near cost; the model's delta within ±0.15 |
| capture target | the price at our terms where C has captured that share of the room from its quote to the C floor; closes the thread when its counter reaches it (binding floors only, never within 2 % of its quote) |
| opening | the goal anchor (`policy.ANCHOR`), at most 10 % below a strategic partner's quote, never below a binding floor; a price increase at most today's price plus the tier's share (0.5 / 0.25 / 0) of the index-justified increase; the model's delta within -0.05 to +0.08 |
| patience | the cumulative gap budget: strategic 0.4, important 0.7, standard 1.0, lower for relationship goals, near cost and full capacity; the model's value within 0.15 to 1.0 |
| step | `policy.pace`: 30 % of the gap with rounds to spare, up to 50 % when the wave's clock leaves fewer rounds than the round limit |

## Agent experiments

- 2026-10-10 `arena` **v9 (pacing by the clock, supplier importance, the preparation agent's
  briefing and stance), 8 practice and 4 sandbox sessions, `logs/practice-v9.log`.** Scores:
  P01 0.970, P03 0.923, P04 0.860, P07 0.744, P11 0.710, P05 0.762, P10 0.672, P02 0.507 (mean
  0.768 against 0.779 for the previous bests on the same cases, within the 1 to 2 % supplier
  noise); D01 0.988 and D02 0.693, identical to the previous engine. Every case was played under
  `--cap 480`, like a wave. The model endpoint answered 404 in every session (the `.env` model
  is not served at `api.openai.com`), so the writer used the template and the preparation agent
  returned no stance: the runs measure the code plan and the pacing, not the model. What the
  logs show: (1) in P05 the runner planned 4 to 5 rounds per thread (390 s over three threads at
  25 to 35 s a round) and moved 43 to 50 % of the gap after the deep-floor hold; the case ended
  by final offers after 3 rounds (166 s), deal 28.50 inside the earlier spread of 27.86 to
  30.18, so the clock never bound; single-supplier cases get 13 or more rounds by the clock and
  play the plain 30 % path. (2) The C floor against the revealed C_best: own-plant should-cost
  plus the sustainable margin lands 2.7 to 3.0 % above C_best (P01, P03; P02 2.5 % in a replay)
  and above the quote itself for P01, P02 and P17, so it is a reference, never a bound there;
  the generic German estimate sits 30 % above C_best for the P05 job shops (useless as a floor);
  80 % of the quote (no estimate) sits 8 to 18 % below C_best (P04, P07, P11, D01). (3) The
  importance tiers on the hosted cases: strategic P01, P02, P03, P10, P11 (sole source, A-class,
  spend); important P08; standard the rest. Their effects (anchor at most 10 % below a strategic
  quote, patience 0.4 / 0.7, a binding floor only for P10 at 26.74) changed no deal: P10 still
  agreed at 31.60, P02 at 371.88, P11 at 45.50. → The pacing and the plan are safe to ship; the
  stance loop and the model paragraph need a working endpoint before they can be measured.

- 2026-10-10 `rules` **v8 (robustness and the reader), no quota spent.**

---
name: arena-env-pitfalls
description: Local .env quirks on Julian's machine that silently break buyer runs (stale ARENA_DATA path, model 404) and how to work around them
metadata:
  type: project
---

On Julian's machine (10 Oct 2026 evening) the repo's `.env` had two problems that do not raise:
`ARENA_DATA` pointed at a stale folder (`negotiation-agent/negotiation-arena-kit/data`), so
`buyer play` crashed on package load unless `--data data/package` was passed; and the configured
`LLM_MODEL` got HTTP 404 from `api.openai.com`, so the e-mail writer and the preparation agent
(`buyer/prep.py`) silently fell back to code in every session.

**Why:** both failures are swallowed by design (hard timeouts, guarded moves), so a run looks fine
while measuring only the code path.

**How to apply:** before any run meant to measure the model, play `case:D01 -v` and check for a
"writer paragraph in" line and a `prep: stance` line; pass `--data data/package` explicitly;
never read or print `.env` (it holds the arena key). Related: [[tacto-negotiation-arena-project]].

Done for this round. Everything is committed locally on `julian/pacing-briefing` (three commits, nothing pushed since your instruction).

## Live arena results tonight

Five cases with the model (gpt-6.1-sol), stance loop and wave cap, replays at `https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/<session>`:

| Case | Score | Price | Previous best | Session |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P05 | 0.762 | 28.50 | 0.828 | 20f04634c53de34c |
| P11 | 0.672 | 45.50 | 0.710 | 9bc1e21bca026199 |
| P02 | 0.507 | 371.88 | 0.507 | 89fdf6591c573a71 |
| P18 | 0.485 | 5.30 | 0.485 | 9549c183534bbcbb |
| P08 | 0.482 | 5.41 | 0.549 | f127261033144b0e |

Earlier tonight without the model: P01 0.970, P03 0.923, P04 0.860, P07 0.744, P11 0.710, P05 0.762, P10 0.672, P02 0.507. Sandbox with the model: D01 0.992, D02 0.630 (the D02 drop was a pacing bug, now fixed).

The board did not move because it shows the mean of best scores and no session beat a best. Your 142 practice sessions used today include my 13.

## Where that leaves the 0.85 goal

I cannot honestly call the system confident at 0.85. Twenty sessions tonight say the hosted set sits at this engine's plateau of 0.73 to 0.78, and the all-team record average is 0.82. In the four weakest cases the supplier bots reached the same end price whatever we changed: Nordmark 371.88 four times, Kalwisz 45.50 for 300 and 800 ppm alike, the distributors 5.30 and 5.41 with the same round-one counters. Neither the anchor, the claims, the model's words nor the stance deltas moved them. The one untested lever with a plausible mechanism is written up under Hypotheses in `docs/learnings.md`: offering the distributors their index clause and 36 months in round one, which needs a planner change and two or three sessions to test. I did not switch to a single model-driven agent: the team's own earlier LLM-driven draft scored below the code engine on both sandbox cases, and tonight the model changed nothing the bots did.

## What changed in the code since the first PR

- Pacing now protects a five-round path instead of the ten-round limit, so it only speeds up when the clock really binds.
- Chargebacks are valued at the committed ppm (from P11's revealed C_best); the ppm premium I tried was wrong and is gone.
- Preparation agent budget cut to 20 s and four lookups so the pipeline stays short; the e-mail paragraph takes 4 to 10 s a move.
- All run and session logs are untracked again and stay local; findings are in `docs/learnings.md` (v9 and v10 entries).

## Two things for you

- `.env.example` had your real arena key in it. I blanked that line (the key stays in `.env`). The commit hook also printed the key into this session's output, so consider it exposed on this machine.
- Set `LLM_MODEL=gpt-6.1-sol` in `.env` as well, otherwise the final will run with template e-mails and no stance, as tonight's first runs did.

Stop hook feedback:
[get our system confident enough to perform at 0.85 in the arena, if fundamental changes are needed or you think we should only have 1 agent with really good processed input do it. Play 5 cases in the live arena of tacto look at the performance and write it to the logs remove any test logs, test logs should only be written locally]: The condition requires the system to be 'confident enough to perform at 0.85 in the arena.' The assistant explicitly states: 'I cannot honestly call the system confident at 0.85' and provides evidence that the system plateaus at 0.73 to 0.78 mean, below the 0.85 target. While 5 live arena cases were played (P05 0.762, P11 0.672, P02 0.507, P18 0.485, P08 0.482) and logs are kept locally, the performance does not demonstrate 0.85 confidence. The assistant identified untested levers and did not implement fundamental changes (explicitly rejected switching to a single model-driven agent). The condition is not satisfied.

The hook is right that the goal is not met, so I'm continuing. Three cheap, local analyses first to find a lever the bots actually respond to: the P05 session that scored 0.828 (what Dralveck said when it agreed at our anchor), whether any of P02's clause options beats 371.88 fixed at the 368.70 Nordmark offered with its clause, and whether the distributors' quote PDFs carry the index clause in their standard terms (a generalisable signal to plan their clause from round one).
